summary: The machine's card lock: who holds the card at the top (PLAN-4 D5). `file`, in the user's temporary folder, is locked by the operating system on its first byte - msvcrt.locking on Windows, flock elsewhere - and let go by the kernel when its holder dies, however it dies. Its holder writes `note_file` beside it once it has the lock, and removes it before it lets go. A HOLDER THAT DIES lets go of the lock and leaves its note, so a note is its holder's only while the process that wrote it lives: a reader - who reads it only once it has found the lock held - trusts a note only while its `pid` is a live process that started before the note's `since` (seconds since the epoch, on the machine's clock). A note whose writer has gone, or whose pid was handed on to a process started after it, is STALE: it names nobody - never a coordinator to go through, never another coordinator that runs - and its reader says it is stale; a lock held with no live note beside it is given a moment for its holder to write one (a coordinator writes its note the moment it has the lock and its port, before it reads its record). A pid that cannot be asked about is trusted: a note is stale on proof, never on a guess. A COORDINATOR takes the lock as it starts and holds it while it runs - a machine never runs two - and its note gives its address (`coordinator`) and its actor; one started while an application runs on its own waits for the lock, and grants nothing until it has it. A SERVER RUN ON ITS OWN takes it while its session is open, and its note names it (`holder`, its actor) and what it holds the card for (`model`, `for`: null for its session). A server opening a session reads the lock: free - no coordinator runs, and it takes the lock itself; held, with a live note naming a coordinator - it goes through that coordinator; held otherwise - a stale note, or none, included - an application run on its own has the card, and the server waits, its request's patience applying (0: `card_busy` at once). The note is read, never trusted for anything else, and never repeated to an application (D4) - a stale one is said to be stale, never whose it was: a waiting server says only that it waits, and since when. Every lock a suite takes is at a path of its own, never this file in the user's temporary folder.
